findings.where: Nav 'Destinations' link (desktop bar and phone menu); footer links 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Report content'
findings.fault: These links go nowhere useful. 'Destinations' points to #destinations, and this page has no such section, so a click does nothing. 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Report content' all point back to this same page. A visitor who asks for the privacy policy, the terms or the way to report content lands where they already were.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who has just read the method and wants to browse destinations hits a dead link. A hostel owner who wants to report or dispute a review, or check the terms, can't. On a page whose whole job is trust, links that don't work undercut the honesty it claims.

findings.where: Final section, 'Hostelworld, for comparison', and the lead's 'instead of calling it proprietary'
findings.fault: The page names a competitor and sets Manta's method against it. It then ends on that competitor, with the line that a hostel 'can look thin there'. The project's own positioning says the claim names no competitor, and the Hostelworld relationship is an open consent ask. The page's last word is a jab at a rival, not Manta's own promise.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose positioning bars naming competitors, especially while the Hostelworld application is pending. A traveller may also read the closing comparison as point-scoring, which weakens the neutral, merit-only stance the page exists to prove.

findings.where: Opening: lead paragraph, the second 'Scores weight toward recent stays…' paragraph, the three-item numbered list, and the first line of 'Ranking method'
findings.fault: The page summarises itself three times before it starts: a large lead, a body-size second summary that reads like a second lead, then a list. 'No hostel can pay for a higher position' then opens the next section word for word. The list is also numbered when it isn't a sequence, so it implies an order or priority that doesn't exist.
findings.who_objects: A phone reader scanning mid-trip spends the first screen reading the same three claims twice. It makes the page feel padded instead of plain.

findings.where: 'Ranking method' section, four unbroken paragraphs (most visible on phone, about one and a half screens)
findings.fault: Four separate topics share one heading with no subheads: whether payment affects rank, pulling thin scores toward the area average, which reviews count and what the badge means, and sorting and zero-review listings. The reader can't jump to the one question they came with.
findings.who_objects: A hostel owner checking whether a partner tier buys rank, or a traveller asking what the reward badge means, has to read the whole block to find their answer.

findings.where: Lead's promise 'This page states it in full', against 'Ranking method' and 'Scoring method'
findings.fault: The page promises the full method but stays vague at the key points. How strongly scores are pulled toward the area average is 'a handful' and 'a few dozen'. 'Our checks' are never described. The fixed word scale every score carries (Loved, Great, Solid, Mixed) and its thresholds are not stated. The page also gives no date the method took effect.
findings.who_objects: A sceptical traveller, or a hostel owner whose score sits near the area average, reads 'in full', then finds no numbers they can check. That is the opposite of the published-method trust the page sells.

findings.fault: The page is a plain column of text on sand: no illustration, no brand moment and no worked example of a score. It reads as a legal notice, which the brand names as its enemy ('sterile/corporate'), and the method is harder to grasp without one picture of a score shifting.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brand sheet calls for 'effortless' as the first feeling and illustration on decorative surfaces. A backpacker who would follow a single visual example of the area-average pull will skim this text without taking it in.

findings.fault: The row wraps right after 'How we rank ·', leaving the dot separator hanging at the end of the first line.
findings.who_objects: Few would notice, but it looks like a slip in an otherwise tidy footer.
